Q: git fetch origin master:master does not advance origin/master, but it does advance FETCH_HEAD A:

I think there's a misunderstanding in how the two commands git fetch origin master and git fetch origin master:master work.

git fetch origin master fetches the master branch from the remote repository and updates the corresponding tracking branch (origin/master) according to the refspec defined for the remote in remote.origin.fetch. The default refspec usually looks like this refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*.

Instead, the command git fetch origin master:master is supplied with a different refspec from the one used by git fetch origin master. This refspec basically says grab the master branch from the remote and update the local master branch (not its remote tracking branch!). The two writings are not the same; git fetch origin +master:refs/remotes/origin/master would be a closer equivalent.

Lastly, as others have already said, the refspec master:master is likely to make the command fail because your local master branch and the remote's master have diverged. Therefore, no update will happen without prefixing the refspec with a + sign. This symbol is needed so that non-fast-forward updates are allowed (if this is what you actually want). Quoting the refspec paragraph from the git fetch docs:

[...] You would want to use the + sign to indicate non-fast-forward updates will be needed for such branches. [...]

Q: Why can removing mutexes in a multithreaded program significantly reduce latency even if contention is low? A:

It might be interesting to run a single-threaded version of your program (where contention is guaranteed to be exactly zero, as only one thread can ever lock the mutex) and see how using/not-using mutexes in that scenario affects the program's latency.

Q: Next js ui Flicker after login A:

This is not a bug in NextAuth or your navbar logic. What you’re seeing is a hydration mismatch caused by resolving the session on the client.

Why the flicker happens

On a full page refresh:

  1. The page is server-rendered first

    • Your Navbar is a client component

    • useSession() has no session yet

    • It renders Login / Register

  2. After hydration on the client:

    • NextAuth fetches /api/auth/session

    • Session becomes available

    • React re-renders → Logout

That brief UI switch is React correcting the UI after hydration.

Important clarification

There is no way for a client component using useSession() to instantly know the auth state on first paint.

So:

  • status === "loading" X

  • skeletons / shimmer X

  • hiding UI X

    all of these are workarounds, not real fixes.

Q: iPhone 14 Pro: External USB mic not available in LiveKit / AVAudioSession call apps, but works in Voice Memos & Instagram Live A:

It appears that this is a documented issue on the Apple forums `videoChat` AVAudioSession.Mode Issues on iPhone 14 Pro Max. Seems like there was a known iOS 16.0 - 16.3 bug specific to iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone Pro Max where VoiceProcessingIO had audio routing issues that didn't affect recording apps using RemoteIO. What iOS version is your iPhone 14 Pro testing device on?

Why does the **same USB mic work in recording apps (Voice Memos, Instagram Live)**but not in call-style apps (LiveKit, WhatsApp, Instagram call)?

So the difference here is that voice memos (when you're just recording, not on a call) use RemoteIO under the hood. VoIP apps like LiveKit, WhatsApp calls, IG calls, etc.. use VoiceProcessingIO instead because they need echo cancellation.

The issue is that VoiceProcessingIO is way pickier about audio routing, when it's active, iOS applies a bunch of extra signal processing to handle echo cancellation and it forces both input and output into voice processing mode.

For your specific use-case, I'd recommend changing your audio mode from default to voiceChat and see if that makes a difference, you could also add allowBluetoothA2DP to your audio category options (not necess:

await AudioSession.setAppleAudioConfiguration({
  audioCategory: 'playAndRecord',
  audioMode: 'voiceChat',
  audioCategoryOptions: ['allowBluetooth', 'defaultToSpeaker'],
});
await AudioSession.startAudioSession();
